description: Energy Policy Simulator (EPS) is a model listed in Open Energy Platform model and framework factsheets, a public register of energy-system model and framework factsheets under the section "Models", published or maintained by not stated on the factsheet. The Energy Policy Simulator (EPS) is a computer model developed by Energy Innovation LLC as part of its Energy Policy Solutions project, an effort which aims to inform policymakers and regulators about which climate and energy policies will reduce greenhouse gas emissions most effectively and at the lowest cost. Coverage: not restricted to one place on the factsheet. Methodical focus: Simulation. The listed link gives the source code or documentation; nothing was downloaded or run. Access is free of charge and open. The licence is GNU General Public License v3.0. Caveats: this record was written from the Open Energy Platform factsheet only, so the code, documentation and any publication it links were not opened, their current availability was not checked, and the factsheet may lag the project. It can support energy-system planning and scenario studies. Related record: the catalogue-level record data-oep-factsheet-catalogue.

outputs: The model reports outputs at annual intervals and provides numerous outputs, including: ->Emissions of 12 different pollutants (CO2, nitrogen oxides (NOx), sulfur oxides (SOx), fine particulate matter (PM2.5), and eight others), as well as carbon dioxide equivalent (CO2e; a measure of the global warming potential of various pollutants). ->Direct cash flow (cost or savings) impacts on consumers, industry (as a whole), government, and several specific industries ->Human deaths avoided thanks to reduced particulate pollution The composition and output of the electricity sector (e.g. capacity and generation from coal, natural gas, wind, solar, etc.) ->Vehicle technology market shares and fleet composition (electric vehicles, etc.) ->Energy use by fuel type from various energy-using technologies (specific types of vehicles, building components, etc.)
